phase1_uncertainty_review.scope: Read-only review of completed Phase-1 uncertainty calculations; this audit file is the only new artifact.
phase1_uncertainty_review.finding: The raw percentile whole-batch bootstrap produces strongly upward-shifted squared-signal intervals in these noise-dominated data. CI-based positivity/resolution claims and derived confidence intervals or lower bounds are not supported.
phase1_uncertainty_review.classification: Statistical-method limitation of the implemented raw percentile bootstrap, not an identified axis, array-shape, or normalization-factor coding error. The requested whole-batch resampling is implemented literally; percentile intervals were an implementation choice, not an explicit user requirement.
phase1_uncertainty_review.estimator: u_hat_sq = (||sum_b S_b||^2 - sum_b Q_b) / (n*(n-1)); S_b sums 40 per-env gradients, Q_b sums their squared norms; B=25, n=1000.
phase1_uncertainty_review.independence_approximation: With independent per-env gradients the expected shift is approximately ((B-1)/B)*trSigma/n. Existing full-batch-normalization and LOO-dependence limitations remain separate.
phase1_uncertainty_review.examples: At theta0 the approximate shift is 18.1 for theory_loo (point 0.483) and 497 for theory_nobase (point 9.07), consistent with the reported intervals lying far above their points.
phase1_uncertainty_review.point_estimates: The audit identifies no additional error in the saved signed point-moment calculations. Point-derived ratios and cosines remain provisional, with their existing dependence assumptions; they must not be described as resolved using these intervals.
phase1_uncertainty_review.gate_scope: B10 in code/gate_features.py verifies synthetic Gaussian point moments within analytic standard errors, not bootstrap confidence-interval coverage.
phase1_uncertainty_review.boundary: Preserve original outputs. A replacement uncertainty method requires a separate approved analysis decision; stored Gram/scalar measurements can support such analysis without additional scientific sampling.

mean_policy: All three planned seeds must provide finite comparable values; no survivor-only means.
